body:
PR #966 (shipped in 1.11.1) disconnected the context-rot handoff gate by removing its entries from each harness plugin's hooks.json. The enforcement CODE was deliberately left intact — that part is correct and must stay — but the code and docs still DESCRIBE THEMSELVES as wired and enforcing. Anyone reasoning from the source, human or agent, concludes the handoff gate is live. It is not. This already cost real debugging time in a live session.

THE DECISION IS ALREADY RECORDED — do not ask, do not re-litigate. #995 asks whether the disconnect is temporary or terminal. #966's own PR body answers it: "The context-rot handoff deny-set is not stable enough YET", it disconnects "WITHOUT deleting the feature or its tests", and "Reconnecting later is a small, easy-to-find revert: flip CONTEXT_ROT_HANDOFF_ENABLED back to true and re-add the two removed hooks.json entries." That is TEMPORARY. Take #995's temporary branch: annotate the sites as DISCONNECTED and KEEP `handoff` in ENFORCING_MODES, with a comment saying why a dead mode stays listed.

VERIFIED AT main (7b261c1e) BEFORE FILING — every one of these is confirmed stale, do not re-verify from scratch, just fix:

  a) plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/hooks.json contains ZERO occurrences of the string "handoff". Both `handoff` AND `handoffstart` are unwired.
  b) adlc-hook.mjs header line 11: `handoff (PreToolUse) -> context-rot deny/handoff (D1-D3) [ENFORCING]` — stale.
  c) adlc-hook.mjs header line 12: `handoffstart (SessionStart) -> continuation context / operator one-liner [advisory]` — ALSO stale, and NOT mentioned in #995. It is unwired too. Fix it in the same pass.
  d) adlc-hook.mjs:2624 comment: "The `rails`/`buildgate`/`handoff` modes are ENFORCING — a crash must FAIL CLOSED" — stale for handoff only.
  e) adlc-hook-run.mjs:23: `ENFORCING_MODES = new Set(['rails','buildgate','handoff'])` — KEEP AS IS, add the why-comment.
  f) adlc-hook-run.mjs:84: `handoff: 10_000, // hooks.json timeout minus buffer` — references a hooks.json entry that no longer exists. Correct the comment; keep the value.
  g) packages/context-handoff/lib/adapter.mjs:673-674: "only Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit/Bash are wired to it — see hooks.json" — unconditionally wrong now, and it is the comment that JUSTIFIES a security guard's scope. Correct it.
  h) plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-handoff-gate.mjs:4: "Codex is an ENFORCING tier: under the deny-set the agent loses structured edits AND the shell wholesale." — #966 covered codex; same drift.
  i) docs/integrations/claude-code.md:144: the context-handoff row says **Enforcing** and "Denies ... and Bash|Shell". Stale.
  j) docs/integrations/pi.md ALSO mentions context-handoff — audit it for the same claim. codex.md / opencode.md were checked and do not carry a context-handoff row, but re-confirm.
  k) `grep -rn 'handoff doctor|ADLC_HANDOFF' docs README.md` returns ZERO hits. The operator recovery path is entirely undocumented.

WHAT TO BUILD

PART 1 — correct the six source sites (b,c,d,e,f,g,h). Annotate as `[DISCONNECTED — see #966]`. Do NOT re-wire anything. Do NOT delete the enforcement implementation.

PART 2 — document the recovery path (#996). Add an operator-facing section covering:
  - `adlc handoff doctor` to list orphaned-unbound markers and their writers
  - `ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY=... adlc handoff doctor --clear --write` to clear them
  - when to use doctor vs `adlc handoff resume` vs a fresh session vs the signed bypass grant. The ORPHANED-UNBOUND case (deny marker with ticket_id:null and content_hash:null) is the doctor case specifically — nothing can ever consume such a marker, so `resume` and "continue in a fresh session", which the deny message itself suggests, DO NOT resolve it.
  - State explicitly that there is NO env kill switch — no ADLC_HANDOFF_BYPASS, no ADLC_HANDOFF_ENFORCEMENT. The only bypass is the signed one-shot grant (.adlc/handoffs/<session>.bypass-grant.json, HMAC-SHA256, requires ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY). This is DELIBERATE and differs from ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS, so say so rather than leaving an operator to grep for a flag that does not exist.
  - Why it matters: under an active deny EVERY Bash call fails closed, including read-only ones. `git status` is denied. `ls` is denied. The agent cannot diagnose its own wedge.

PART 3 — THE ACTUAL FIX: a drift guard so this cannot silently recur. Correcting the prose alone leaves the next disconnect free to re-create exactly this state. Add scripts/test/handoff-wiring-drift.test.mjs, in the style of the existing repo-level guards in scripts/test/ (flag-consistency, ceremony-drift, p6-close-step-docs):
  - parse the set of verbs actually wired in plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/hooks.json
  - assert every mode annotated [ENFORCING] in adlc-hook.mjs's header block IS wired there
  - assert every mode in ENFORCING_MODES that is NOT wired carries a DISCONNECTED annotation naming an issue
  - assert docs/integrations/claude-code.md does not describe an unwired verb as **Enforcing**
  - the guard must go RED against the current (pre-fix) tree and GREEN after. Show both.
  Parse structurally, not by string equality — a prose rewording must not red it, a false claim must.

RAILS: plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/hooks.json and packages/context-handoff/lib/mutation-gate.mjs. This ticket corrects DESCRIPTIONS. If either the wiring or the D1-D3 gate logic changes, the work has gone wrong — this is not the re-wiring ticket.

ACCEPTANCE
- The drift guard fails on the pre-fix tree and passes after; both outputs shown in the PR.
- `npm test` green from the repo root, output shown.
- `adlc rails-guard --base origin/main --ticket <this ticket id>` exits 0, proving hooks.json and mutation-gate.mjs were untouched.
- `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs` exits 0 on the diff.
- A grep proving zero remaining [ENFORCING] annotations on unwired verbs, and that `handoff doctor` now appears in docs.
title: handoff gate: stop the source and docs claiming enforcement after #966 disconnected it (#995, #996)
